column1: # .github/timer-audit.tsv - every periodic tick and every credential lifetime
# in this tree, classified, each naming the fact behind it.
# principles.md: a state change follows a checkable FACT, never a clock. A
# timeout is allowed on a single I/O call. A periodic tick is allowed as a
# safety net that RE-CHECKS a fact. Every unavoidable bound needs a comment
# That rule is easy to agree with and easy to lose. Each of the bounds below was
# added for a reason that made sense where it was written; what nothing recorded
# was which KIND it is, and therefore whether the fact behind it still exists.
#   tick       a periodic construct that re-checks a fact. `fact` names it.
#   ttl        a credential lifetime. `fact` names what it is a safety net
#              over, or the word `none` - and then `cite` must say where that
#              is recorded, because a credential whose validity the clock
#              decides on its own IS clock-driven state.
#   io-bound   a bound on one I/O call, which principles.md allows outright.
#   retention  neither: a cache or data-retention bound that decides no
#              credential's validity and no state transition.
# The `fact` column is the point of the file. A row that names no fact is a
